package.title: Does AI break the case for broad index investing? Rent decay, private capital, and deflation

article.journal: The Journal of Beta Investment Strategies

package.data_as_of: Fund returns January 2018 to September 2026; return on capital by industry January 2026; sector weights and index concentration October 2026; index membership to August 2026; annual asset returns 1928 to 2025.
package.units: Returns, volatilities, drawdowns, weights and returns on capital are in per cent. Counts are whole numbers. The `fields` entry of this header says what each key means.

licence.condition: Reuse of the results is allowed with credit to the paper.
licence.third_party_data: The inputs come from Aswath Damodaran (NYU Stern), Portfolio Visualizer, BlackRock iShares, the US Treasury, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics and others. data/README.md lists the source and the terms of each file. Third-party data remain the property of their sources, are included for replication with attribution, and are not covered by the licence above.

package.cite_package: Papadogiannis, A. (2026). Does AI break the case for broad index investing? Rent decay, private capital, and deflation. Replication package, version 1.1.0. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24240516

fields.exhibit5_roic_by_layer: one record per layer of scarcity: `layer`; `industries` and `firms`, the number of US industries and firms in it; `roic`, the median after-tax return on invested capital, in per cent; `roic_adj`, the same adjusted for leases and R&D; `roic10`, the ten-year normalised figure
fields.exhibit6_sector_composition.groups: share of market value in each group of sectors, in per cent, as a list in the order US, developed ex-US, emerging, world
fields.exhibit6_sector_composition.slow: summed share, in the same order, of three groups: financials and health care; energy, materials, utilities and real estate; industrials
fields.exhibit6_sector_composition.region: weight of each region in the world index, in per cent, under the keys US, DevexUS (developed markets outside the US), EM (emerging markets) and World
fields.exhibit7_fund_returns: by fund ticker. `post_` figures cover the AI period, December 2022 to September 2026; `full_` figures cover January 2018, or the fund's first month if later, to September 2026. `_ann` is the compound annual total return, `_vol` the annualised standard deviation of monthly returns, `_dd` the largest fall from a peak on month-end values, all in per cent. `n_full` is the number of months in the full period
fields.exhibit8_membership_concentration.adds_p: average number of companies added to the S&P 500 a year, by five-year period
fields.exhibit8_membership_concentration.surviv: by year: the number of S&P 500 members at the end of that year, then how many of them were still members in August 2026
fields.exhibit8_membership_concentration.top10,: summed weight of the 10 and of the 50 largest S&P 500 constituents on 20 October 2026, in per cent
fields.exhibit8_membership_concentration.vt_top: weight of the ten largest holdings of the Vanguard Total World Stock ETF, in per cent, and its number of holdings, on 30 September 2026
fields.exhibit9_real_yield_sensitivity: by fund ticker: `beta`, the fund's monthly return in per cent per one-point rise in the 10-year Treasury real yield in the same month (least squares); `t`, its t-statistic with Newey-West standard errors, three lags; `r2`; `n`, the number of months
fields.exhibit10_inflation_regimes: by inflation regime: `n`, the number of years from 1928 to 2025 in it; `stocks`, `tbill`, `tbond`, the average real yearly return of the S&P 500, 3-month Treasury bills and 10-year Treasury bonds in those years, in per cent; `n72`, the number of years from 1972; `gold`, the average real yearly return of gold in those years, null where there is none
